### Remember God’s Promises
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/today-s-insight-september-30-2013.html
Passage: Psalm 137:4-6
Points:
- The psalmist turns inward to ask how captive exiles can authentically sing the Lord's song in a foreign land.
- Genuine, joyful worship cannot be compelled by oppressors or sustained by guilt; it requires supernatural freedom.
- Despite the severe chastisement of exile, the psalmist refuses to abandon hope in God's covenant promises.
- Pledging that his hand and tongue lose their function before forgetting Jerusalem personalizes the community's commitment to God.
- Believers enduring the painful fallout of past failure can remain confident that God's bond with them is unbreakable.

### What Do We Do with Psalm 137?
Author: Aaron Armstrong
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/what-do-we-do-with-psalm-137-bible-study-minute-september-20-2017.html
Passage: Psalm 137:7-9
Points:
- The severe imprecations in the psalm represent a plea for divine justice rather than an appeal to personal vengeance.
- In seasons of deep grief, God's people are called to remember both their loss and His promise of ultimate deliverance.
- The gospel offers the supreme resolution to divine wrath, as Christ endured terrible suffering to set believers free.
- Earthly afflictions and trials test believers, but they serve to shape them into the image of Christ.
- Christians should acknowledge and mourn their trials without allowing despair to overpower their hope in God's promises.
